title: Chapter test: Enums and Pattern Matching
summary: Ten questions on enums, Option, match, if let and let...else. You need 70% to pass; you can retry and your best score is kept.

questions.q: Which type models "a payment is either cash, a card with its last four digits, or a voucher with a code"?
options: `struct Payment { cash: bool, card: u16, voucher: String }`
questions.explanation: One of several alternatives, each with its own data: an enum.

questions.code:
let x: Option<u8> = None;
println!("{}", x.map(|v| v * 2).unwrap_or(7));
questions.explanation: `map` on `None` stays `None`, and `unwrap_or` gives the default.

questions.q: In Rust, any reference or variable can be null.
questions.explanation: Rust has no null; a possibly missing value has type `Option<T>`.

questions.q: What is wrong with this match?
options: The `0` arm can never run, because `_` catches everything first
questions.explanation: Arms are tried in order; the compiler warns that the second arm is unreachable.
The guard fails for -3, it is not 0, so `Some(_)` matches.

questions.q: Which can follow `=>` in a match arm?
questions.explanation: Any expression works, including blocks and nested matches.

questions.q: What does `if let Some(n) = s.find('x') { ... } else { ... }` do when `s` has no `x`?
options: Runs the first block with n = 0

questions.explanation: The else block must diverge (leave). Printing alone does not leave.

questions.q: The error code for a match that misses a case is E000___ (one digit).
A `match` on an `i32` has the arms `0 =>`, `1..=9 =>`, `n if n < 0 =>` and `_ =>`. Where must `_ =>` go?
options: It is not needed because the other arms cover everything
questions.explanation: The catch-all matches everything, so any arm after it would be unreachable. The other three cover only some integers, so `_` is required.
